searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he atomic implementation matrix the awtsmoos renews the whole through exact deeds, each small vessel receiving its measure; awtsmoos.com turns brainstorm into code, proof, documentation, and release treasure. parallel lane a — state and docs reconciliation 1. inspect whether the uncertain three doc rewrite landed. 2. compare docs against current lifecycle/package/browser evidence. 3. rewrite only stale docs as whole files. 4. add decision table, troubleshooting, performance evidence. 5. update evidence ledger, remaining work, next action. parallel lane b — lifecycle/core edge cases 1. inspect existing input/seed/request tests. 2. add lifecycle parity tests for malformed json, tojson, authored seed, request override. 3. add explanation purity execution counter test. 4. run focused lifecycle + existing facade lanes. 5. fix core only if a test exposes a real semantic mismatch. parallel lane c — compiler/constraint/cache hardening 1. inspect registry duplicate behavior and cache identity sources. 2. add cache invalidation tests for compiler version/support state and solver plan changes. 3. add environment dependent solver bypass and compile failure cache tests. 4. add overlapping compiler coverage determinism test if architecture supports a stable rule. 5. document any deliberately unspecified ordering rather than inventing it. parallel lane d — demo ux/accessibility 1. add home/end and editable/modifier shortcut guard. 2. add lifecycle workspace busy state and completion announcement. 3. add local compile duration, pipeline support counts, primitive count, lightweight badge. 4. bound public error text. 5. keep every module <=120 lines by splitting renderers/state helpers. 6. add tests after full source draft. parallel lane e — browser/security/responsive proof 1. re run 390px e2e after any demo source changes. 2. add 320px viewport proof. 3. assert no external origin resources. 4. assert no exceptions/console errors/severe logs. 5. test unknown scenario query fallback. 6. test home/end and editable key guard. parallel lane f — git/release ownership 1. refresh head/origin/concurrent status. 2. build exact mission file manifest from status/import dependencies. 3. identify any mission dependency hidden among concurrent dirty files. 4. inspect release scripts/authority and exact commands. 5. do not stage until all source/test/doc/browser gates are green. 6. stage explicit paths, inspect staged diff, verify clean integration worktree, push exact sha, activate, public e2e. completion condition every accepted source change has tests, docs, runtime evidence, and ownership evidence. every deferred idea is documented as deliberately deferred rather than forgotten. github and production exact sha proof must close before remaining work becomes empty.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he chesed maximal improvement wave the awtsmoos renews every hidden seam before the seam can know its name; awtsmoos.com pours possibility without limit, then focused regression universe after the final test splits, not before. 3. re run the existing universal facade/compiler/constraint/default compiler universe beside it. 4. re run the recursive lifecycle compare only new reds against the independently proven baseline. 7. start a fresh local static server after focused tests are green. 8. launch a new cache busted chrome target rather than reusing earlier page state. 9. verify unknown scenario query falls back to the first scenario and rewrites the canonical query. 10. verify arrowleft and arrowright wrap and focus correctly. 11. verify home selects/focuses the first scenario and end selects/focuses the last. 12. verify ctrl/meta/alt/shift modified navigation keys do nothing. 13. verify keys dispatched from input/textarea/select/contenteditable do nothing. 14. verify rapid scenario selection cannot let an old async generation overwrite the latest generation. 15. verify lifecycle workspace aria busy true during work and false when complete. 16. verify polite status announcement reports completion. 17. verify root data state moves loading/compiling ready. 18. verify nine summary cards exist and include local compile time, primitive count, pipeline support counts. 19. verify every scenario still produces exactly one svg artifact and 15 pipeline stages. 20. verify unresolved constraint counts remain truthful for each of the five authored worlds. 21. verify compile again exposes miss hit reuse in public status. 22. verify 320px css viewport has no page level horizontal overflow. 23. verify 390px css viewport has no page level horizontal overflow. 24. verify very long budget/hash/compiler/solver text remains contained at both widths. 25. verify every network resource is same origin. 26. verify no runtime exceptions, console errors, or severe browser logs. 27. measure current v3 demo js/core module count and compare to the lifecycle static graph. 28. re run deterministic cache microbenchmark after cache identity tests settle. 29. verify failed compilation leaves cache statistics honest. 30. verify environment dependent solver bypass produces no accidental cache entry. 31. verify compiler remains executor free on the lifecycle facade. 35. verify malformed json/wrapper/seed/request precedence parity on lifecycle facade. 36. verify package subpath import itself remains direct to the lightweight module. 37. inspect package export ordering and accidental duplicate keys. 38. inspect public universal index for accidental world imports through the lightweight subpath. 39. inspect all new demo renderers for innerhtml/eval/network regressions. 40. inspect all new error surfaces for host paths/secrets leaking to public text. 41. inspect all touched source/test files for cramped one line functions or hidden space indentation. 42. inspect all touched docs for claims stronger than measured evidence. 43. create a current evidence ledger entry with exact test/browser job ids. 44. create planned vs actual delta from plans 18 23 and actual files/results. 45. search for todo/fixme/xxx/placeholder markers in mission owned files. 46. search for accidental dead/unreferenced new modules. 47. search for duplicate demo responsibility after the latest split. 48. search for any public route or package documentation still showing only full createawtsmoos. 49. search for stale version 2 demo assumptions in tests/docs. 50. search for stale 6 summary card assumptions after v3 summary expansion. 51. build an exact mission file manifest before staging. 52. classify every mission adjacent dirty file as required, unrelated, or uncertain. 53. refresh head, origin/main, branch, and remote just before integration. 54. fetch origin and calculate divergence at that exact in the clean integration worktree. 58. run package self reference/import graph in the clean integration worktree. 59. serve the demo from the integration worktree and browser smoke it before commit/push if practical. 60. inspect full staged diff in integration worktree. 61. commit one coherent universal lifecycle/demo tranche. 62. push exact commit sha to origin/main only after fresh fetch/fast forward safety proof. 63. verify remote main sha via ls remote. 64. re read bhrelease prepare contract immediately before deployment. 65. run prepare phase only from the clean exact integration worktree. 66. run activate phase only with the exact pushed sha. 67. verify production worktree head and origin/main equal the intended sha. 68. verify canonical server activation receipt/status. 69. fresh browser public https://awtsmoos.com/apps/universal procedural/. 70. repeat the local browser contract publicly: five scenarios, cache hit, 15 stages, navigation, narrow widths, no severe logs. 71. verify public resources are same origin and lifecycle module graph remains light. 72. verify public html advertises version 3 and lifecycle composition. 73. verify public server revision/authority evidence identifies intended release sha when infrastructure exposes it. 74. update api/migration/performance docs with final v3 browser measurements. 75. update evidence ledger with release/public proof. 76. update remaining work after each gate; do not empty it merely because code is green. 77. update next action after each gate; execute it while safe. 78. re read every mission owned file after integration and compare planned vs actual one last time. 79. run embarrassment test: what would a user notice immediately as unfinished? 80. run takeover test: what would a new developer do first? 81. run hidden dependency search again after integration because origin/main moved. 82. run hidden test search again after integration because fresh upstream may add relevant coverage. 83. re run architecture/import graph if upstream changes touch universal api infrastructure. 84. preserve historical baseline reds rather than silently rewriting unrelated work. 85. clean local static server/browser targets only after evidence is copied into durable ledger. 86. remove temporary clean worktrees only after remote/public proof is preserved. 87. ensure docs do not promise typed dependency scheduling that does not exist. 88. ensure docs do not promise subgraph incremental cache that does not exist. 89. ensure demo never implies svg is canonical semantic output. 90. ensure lifecycle/full factories continue sharing one awtsmoos implementation, not forked logic.

title: Gevurah Release Critique
excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Gevurah Release Critique The Awtsmoos renews restraint together with abundance, drawing the line where truth can live; Awtsmoos.com rejects ornamental labor when evidence says the wiser act is to verify, integrate, and give. searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he gevurah release critique the awtsmoos renews restraint together with abundance, drawing the line where truth can live; awtsmoos.com rejects ornamental labor when evidence says the wiser act is to verify, integrate, and give. critique of the maximal wave do not add new semantic authorities merely to increase feature count. the lifecycle/full split already solves the proven composition problem. do not change cache implementation unless the new behavioral tests reveal a real identity or failure policy defect. do not add browser timing slas. record local measurements, but keep structural graph/resource contracts as the stable guarantee. do not invent typed dependency scheduling from string dependency ids; current ids can represent services. do not add csp or deployment headers until production header ownership is traced; a local meta policy can break legitimate module imports. do not alter unrelated 19 baseline failures to manufacture a green full suite number. do not stage from the dirty primary checkout. fresh origin integration worktree is mandatory. do not replay any old uncertain mutation; inspect current files and git diff instead. do not push until every mission file has been explicitly classified and the staged diff is inspected. do not deploy a sha that differs from remote main or from the clean release worktree head. highest value order 1. finish focused test verification on the final split files. 2. fix only evidence backed regressions. 3. run existing universal + structural + package/import graph gates. 4. run full package suite and classify differences against historical baseline. 5. run fresh v3 browser e2e at 320/390 with navigation, race, busy/live, same origin, and diagnostic assertions. 6. refresh docs/evidence with final measurements. 7. generate planned vs actual delta and exact mission file manifest. 8. integrate in fresh origin clean worktree. 9. test staged/integrated state again. 10. commit, push exact sha, verify origin. 11. prepare/activate through audited two phase release. 12. public e2e and exact sha verification. 13. only then close remaining work. risks demanding special proof upstream main moved while this mission was in progress. the primary checkout has unrelated concurrent dirty work. browser resource counts can change as the v3 demo adds small modules; module count changes are evidence, not necessarily regressions. rapid async interaction can expose stale render races even when normal clicks pass. test generation files themselves previously crossed the 120 line ceiling, proving structural gates must include tests. public deployment can succeed mechanically while serving stale cache/state; fresh browser and cache busted requests remain mandatory.
